what: DERIVATION, independent attempt 3 of 4: The force between two capturing bodies in the collisionless limit, exactly. SETTING (blocks 43 and 44; open PRs titled 'ail43: the fields of the record layer arrive by diffusion' and 'ail44: records with inertia'): block 43 showed that the two fields found in the record layer settle by a random walk (a distance R costs about R^2 ticks), so a carrier of a long-range field needs a speed. BLOCK 44's CLAUSE (supplied, not adopted): a record's content is its direction of travel. (S) each record at rate 1 tries to step along its content (six-axis menu: to x + e_d; sphere menu: to x + e_k with probability max(0, s.e_k)/sqrt 3); an empty target is entered; an occupied target exchanges contents with the record (the two pass through each other); a solid site reflects it. (C) each bond at rate gamma re-draws the contents of its two records uniformly on their momentum class (six axes: an opposite pair becomes a uniformly random opposite pair, any other pair is exchanged with probability 1/2; sphere: P/2 +- r w, w uniform on the unit circle orthogonal to P = s + s', r^2 = 1 - |P|^2/4). PROVED: number of records and momentum (sum of the contents' unit vectors) are conserved by every event; the clause is covariant; the UNIFORM measure is stationary (every record has exactly one streaming preimage; the scattering kernel is symmetric), also with reflecting bodies, and NOT if blocked attempts do nothing or if head-on pairs scatter when an attempt is blocked; in product states the mass current is (1 - rho) g and the pressure is exactly rho/3, so the linearized Euler speed squared is (1 - rho)/3 (six axes) and (1 - rho)/9 (sphere); in equilibrium the mean force on a reflecting body is exactly zero. EXECUTED: standing waves oscillate at 0.467 vs 0.483 (six axes) and 0.277 vs 0.279 (sphere) at density 0.3; bodies that CAPTURE records attract each other; bodies that emit records were also measured. The simulators are probes/lib/inertial.py (both menus: tick6, tick_s, sound) and probes/lib/inertial_bodies.py (two bodies in the sphere-menu gas: usage inertial_bodies.py L rho0 radius separation Q ticks seed gamma [absorb] [single]). TASK: in the limit of low density the inertial gas is a set of independent streaming records. (a) Six-axis menu: two capturing bodies A and B; show that the force of B on A is the momentum flux B removes from the streams that would have hit A: nonzero only if the projections of A and B along a lattice axis overlap, equal to j times the overlap area (j the flux per site per direction), independent of the separation: beams, no inverse-square law. (b) Sphere menu with streaming probabilities max(0, s.e_k)/sqrt 3: compute the angular distribution of the records arriving at a site from a distant uniform reservoir, the flux shadowed by a distant body of cross-section A_B, and the force on A: show F = C j A_A A_B / r^2 for r much larger than the bodies and give the constant C for this lattice streaming rule (is the arrival distribution isotropic?). (c) Additivity: for porous bodies of N records each (every record of the body captures), the force in the dilute limit is proportional to N_A N_B; find the opacity at which it saturates to the cross-section. (d) Emitting bodies in the same limit: repulsion, with the same distance law; give it. check.py: exact ray counting on a lattice for small bodies.  DELIVERABLE, in your unit worktree on ai/probes: probes/work/derive/shadow-force-dilute-exact/<your worker name>/ATTEMPT.md and check.py. ATTEMPT.md: (1) the exact statement you attempt; (2) numbered steps, each marked PROVED (argument given in full), CHECKED (a finite fact check.py verifies exactly) or ASSUMED; (3) if the route fails, the FIRST step that fails and why: a precise no-go for a route is a result; (4) what would finish it. check.py: exact arithmetic (fractions, integers, sympy) for every finite claim; it prints `SUMMARY: PROVED ...`, `SUMMARY: COUNTEREXAMPLE ...`, `SUMMARY: PARTIAL <what is new and exact>` or `SUMMARY: ROUTE FAILS AT <step>`, and a line `HIT: <the claim>` ONLY when you claim a proof, a counterexample, or a new exact partial result others can build on; a HIT is handed to a worker of another model family to referee line by line, so write for a hostile reader. Rules: definitions come from the notes on the PR branches named above (git fetch origin <branch>; git show origin/<branch>:<note>; find them with gh pr view <n> --json files,headRefName); any outside theorem you use must be re-proved at the scope you use it or listed under ASSUMED; no status words (proved theorems are promoted by the supervisor after the referee). Have your own plan BEFORE reading the prior attempts printed at claim time; then either build on a refereed partial result or take a different route. Run: python3 probes/run_probe.py <task> --worker <name> --model <model> --review "..." --extra "python3 probes/work/derive/shadow-force-dilute-exact/<name>/check.py"
